metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The only inherited point is the linked city Coquimbo Q3871 at longitude -71.338, latitude -29.9532. The institutional account establishes an air attack on ships in Coquimbo Bay, but supplies no surveyed point or calibrated battle chart. Remove the city locator without substituting a bay centre, present harbour facility, observer location or museum address; the engagement position remains unresolved.

inclusionReview.note: Individually reviewed inclusion of the air attack on the mutinous Chilean squadron in Coquimbo Bay on 6 September 1931. The Chilean national heritage museum reproduces eyewitness accounts of fighting between government aircraft and the ships and distinguishes the roughly half-hour action from the wider naval mutiny. The date is retained: the museum-hosted chapter p.171 explicitly places the action on Sunday 6 September; the short web article’s Saturday wording is a weekday typo. This does not promote the broad naval-warfare class. The city coordinate inherited from Coquimbo Q3871 is withdrawn by the companion metadata review. No fleet-wide revolt total, aircraft-versus-ship ratio, losses or precise ship position is inferred. The existing Q5722370 homonym is a separate Uruguayan battle, not this Chilean action.

note:
The two sourced groups describe the government aircraft and the mutinous ships in the 6 September 1931 Coquimbo Bay encounter. Their media remain separate. Strength, deaths and casualties are unknown here: no all-revolt fleet total or total navy personnel are assigned to this action, no aircraft count is compared with ships, and no damage or forced landing is treated as a destroyed vessel. No equipment profile or polity identity is inferred for these local groups. Published narratives disagree on aircraft strength and damage; those observations are not converted into a single accepted count.
